correctness.rationale: Residue fibers \(C_a\) all have size \(s\), and distinct \(x\in C_a,y\in C_b\) are adjacent exactly when \(a+b\ne0\) in the residue field. In characteristic two each fiber is independent and all distinct fibers are completely joined, so the ordinary and total formulas reduce to the known complete-multipartite support counts. In odd characteristic, \(C_0\) is independent, each nonzero \(C_a\) is a clique, opposite fibers \(C_a,C_{-a}\) have no cross edges, and every other pair is completely joined. Every set meeting at least two fibers dominates; total domination fails exactly for a set supported on one nonzero opposite pair when one selected side has size one, yielding the displayed correction term. The reconstruction from \(D\) by the highest coefficient differing from \((1+x)^N\) correctly separates characteristic two from odd characteristic and recovers \(s\) and \(q=N/s\).
correctness.risk: The theorem is confined to finite commutative local rings; nonlocal residue products do not have the same one-fiber/opposite-pair support classification.

originality.rationale: The final formulas are routine specializations of prior general graph-polynomial theorems once the standard residue-fiber structure of local unit graphs is recognized. A local unit graph is an \(H\)-join over the residue classes: the base graph has \(a\sim b\) exactly when \(a+b\ne0\), and the fiber graph is empty in residue characteristic two, while in odd characteristic it is empty at \(a=0\) and complete at \(a\ne0\). Subramanian--Selvakumar already characterize all total dominating sets and give the total-domination polynomial for arbitrary \(H\)-join graphs; Selvakumar--Manikandan--Murugan do the same for ordinary domination in the more general \(H\)-generalized-join setting. The characteristic-two ordinary and total formulas are even written explicitly in those papers for complete multipartite graphs. The submitted residue-parity formulas follow by direct substitution/support enumeration, and the reconstruction statement is then a short coefficient inspection. Under the rule that stronger prior coverage and direct corollaries count as covered, the final claim does not clear originality.
